title: The Civic Time Expansion Era
summary: A near future in which cities treated spare hours as public infrastructure, issuing extra weekdays through experimental municipal machines.

title: A paper Monday drops
body: It is warm from the machine and already annotated with chores you do not remember accepting. By noon, the borrowed day begins collecting interest in unfinished plans.

title: The machine keeps humming
body: Somewhere inside, an extra weekday remains unsold. The corridor feels briefly spacious, and your untouched weekend survives as a small act of resistance.

title: The Vending Machine That Sells Extra Mondays
accessionNote: Recovered from the abandoned Municipal Office of Calendar Expansion.
summary: A brushed-steel vending machine hums beside a locked gallery door, promising one more Monday to anyone willing to pay in plans.
artifactLabel: The selector glass is cracked. Behind it, tiny calendar pages rotate like candy coils, each stamped with a date that never entered the official year.
visualDescription: A battered steel vending machine stands under museum lights. Its cracked selector window displays miniature calendar pages coiled like snacks behind smudged glass.
